How the Free Roofing Line Works

One call, a few questions, and a transfer to an independent roofing company that works in your part of Dallas-Fort Worth. Here is exactly what happens, and what the line does not do.

Call (469) 649-7066 Walk through a call
  1. Home
  2. How It Works

A call, from start to finish

Most calls take two or three minutes. Here is the order of things, using a typical spring evening in North Texas as the example: hail went through an hour ago, and there is now a brown ring on the upstairs ceiling.

  1. You dial (469) 649-7066. The automated assistant picks up immediately, whatever the hour.
  2. It asks what kind of help you need. The number serves roofing, air conditioning and heating, and pressure washing, so the first question sorts your call. Say roofing.
  3. It asks about the roof. In a sentence or two: hail, a leak, missing shingles, a tree limb, a worn-out roof, a commercial building. It also asks your town and how urgent it is.
  4. It transfers you. The line rings through to a locally owned, independent roofer working in your part of DFW. Before it picks up, the company hears a short summary of what you said, so you do not have to start over.
  5. If the company cannot answer, your name, callback number, town, need and urgency are passed to it so it can call you back.
  6. From there you deal with the roofer. It sets a time to look at the roof, inspects it, gives you its own estimate, and if you hire it, does the work. You pay it directly, or your insurer pays as you arrange.

What the line does, and what it never does

The line does

  • Answer every call with an automated assistant, day and night
  • Ask a few questions so the roofer knows what to expect
  • Transfer you, or pass your details for a call back
  • Publish guides on hail, permits, costs and Texas claim law

The line never

  • Climbs on a roof, inspects, quotes, repairs, replaces or tarps
  • Sells shingles or any other product
  • Files, negotiates or manages insurance claims
  • Charges you, or promises anything about a company's work, price or schedule

Why it is set up this way

After a big hailstorm, homeowners across Dallas-Fort Worth face the same problem at once: hundreds of roofing companies, signs in every yard, crews knocking on doors, and no simple way to know who is local. A single number that reaches a locally owned company cuts down the searching.

The line is paid the way many referral services are: companies that receive calls may pay it a referral fee. That keeps the call free for you. It also means you should treat the connection as a starting point, not an endorsement. Ask the questions on the roofer checking guide no matter who you hire.

Good questions for the roofer who calls you

  • Do you charge to come out and look at the roof?
  • Will you send a certificate of liability insurance from your insurance agent?
  • Does my city require a permit or contractor registration, and who pulls the permit?
  • Can I have the estimate in writing, with the shingle brand and line, decking price and warranty?
  • Who will be on my roof: your own employees or a subcontracted crew?
  • What payment do you expect, and when?

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Questions about the line itself

Is a person or a machine on the other end?

A recorded, automated assistant, round the clock. First it sorts the call (the number also serves heating, cooling and pressure washing), then it asks for a sentence about the roof and your town. It does not diagnose the roof or give prices. Its job is to get you to a roofing company quickly. If you would rather write than talk, use the contact form.

Do roofing companies pay the line?

They may. A roofer that gets calls can owe DFW Expert Roofers a fee per referral, and the site says so on every page. You pay the line nothing, and the fee is not a reason to hire anyone. Compare the roofer's written estimate with others if you like, and confirm its insurance and permits on your own, as the roofer checking guide explains.

Who to call for a leaky roof in the middle of the night?

You can call this line; it answers overnight and rings you through to a roofer serving your part of town. Night visits are that roofer's call and the weather's, since nobody can safely work on a roof in lightning or heavy rain. In the meantime, catch the water indoors and stay off the roof. See emergency roof repair and tarping.

Am I obligated to hire the company I am connected with?

No. Being connected costs nothing and commits you to nothing. Listen to what the roofer finds, read its written estimate, and decide. If something feels wrong, such as pressure to sign that day or an offer to cover your deductible, you can end the conversation and call the line again later.

Does the line check the roofing companies?

No. The line does not license, inspect, certify or rate the companies, and it cannot vouch for anyone's insurance or work. Texas has no state roofing license, so do your own checks before you sign: an insurance certificate from the insurer, a written contract, the city permit, and nearby addresses you can drive past. The FAQ has more on this.

Ready to try it? The call is free

Say what the roof is doing and which town you are in. The automated assistant passes you to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in DFW. That company comes out, looks at the roof and prices the job itself.

  • Costs you nothingThe line sends no bill. Any price you hear comes from the roofer, and you can ask for it on paper.
  • Check before you hireTexas issues no roofing license, so ask for an insurance certificate, a written contract and the permit your city requires.
